pages.title: Building a Heat Exchanger
pages.text: The example below is $(thing)5 x 5 x 5$(), with one straight condenser run and one straight evaporator run side by side.$(br2)Press the eye button to project it into the world.

pages.name: Basic Heat Exchanger
pages.text: Two straight channel runs, each capped by a Fluid Port at both ends. The terminal sits on the wall beside them.

pages.title: Channel rules
pages.text: Every channel block must have exactly $(thing)two$() connections, no more and no less. A straight line satisfies that, and so does a snake as long as it never branches.$(br2)Each run has to begin at a Fluid Port and end at another one. Four ports total: two condenser, two evaporator.

pages.title: Getting more out of it
pages.text: Heat moves faster when the two runs sit next to each other, so weave them rather than putting them in opposite corners.$(br2)Longer runs mean more contact and more throughput, which is why a snaking layout beats a straight one in anything larger than this example.

pages.title: Hooking it up
pages.text: Set one port on each run to Inlet and the other to Outlet.$(br2)For a condenser loop: turbine exhaust into the condenser inlet, water out of the condenser outlet and back to the reactor. Whatever you want to heat goes through the evaporator side.
